about: Modular is a Palo Alto AI infrastructure company, founded in 2022 by Chris Lattner, the creator of LLVM and Swift, and Tim Davis, that builds the Mojo programming language and the MAX platform for running AI models across different hardware. It sells to developers, AI companies and cloud providers, earning from software and enterprise licences. Backed by General Catalyst, GV and others, Crunchbase shows about 380 million dollars raised, with a valuation of 1.6 billion dollars. A developer-focused B2B brand with a following in the AI engineering community.

Couchbase is a software company, founded in 2008 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California, listed here with a San Jose address, that sells a NoSQL cloud database platform, including Couchbase Capella, for building web, mobile and AI applications. Customers include large banks, airlines and retailers, and revenue is from subscriptions of around 200 million dollars a year. It listed on Nasdaq as BASE in 2021 and agreed to be taken private by Haveli Investments in 2025. A B2B developer brand with little consumer awareness.

Krutrim is an Indian artificial intelligence company based in Bengaluru, founded in 2023 by Bhavish Aggarwal, who also founded Ola, building large language models for Indian languages, cloud services, an AI assistant and custom AI chips. It became India's first AI unicorn in early 2024 after a funding round. Customers include developers and companies, plus consumers who use the Krutrim app, and Crunchbase shows about 304 million dollars raised. A visible Indian tech brand tied to Ola's founder.

SK ecoplant is a South Korean construction and engineering company in Seoul, part of SK Group, formerly SK Engineering and Construction. It builds civil works, plants and housing, and has moved into environmental businesses such as waste-to-energy, hydrogen and data centres. Listed on the Korea Exchange (SK ecoplant, 2021 IPO). Customers are governments and corporations. Revenue is several trillion won. B2B contractor with moderate brand recognition in Korea.

ScaleOps is a New York-based Israeli-founded start-up that automates Kubernetes resource management in real time, reducing cloud spend for engineering teams. Founded in 2022, it raised about 210 million dollars across rounds led by Insight Partners. Customers are companies running Kubernetes at scale. B2B software with a niche audience in cloud engineering. It sells to cloud engineering teams, so awareness is strong among DevOps staff but nil among consumers.

Zenity is a New York-based AI security and governance platform that helps enterprises protect AI agents, copilots and low-code applications from misuse and data leaks. Founded in Israel in 2021, it has raised about 185 million dollars. Customers are large enterprises and security teams. B2B cybersecurity vendor with a niche but growing profile. It sells to security teams that need to govern AI use inside their organisations, with a focus on large enterprises.

Altera Infrastructure, formerly Teekay Offshore, is a Bermuda-registered offshore energy services company based in Hamilton, owned by Brookfield. It owns and operates shuttle tankers, floating production storage and offloading units (FPSOs), floating storage units and towage vessels for oil companies, especially in the North Sea and Brazil. It restructured through a Chapter 11 process in 2022. Customers are oil majors and national oil companies. B2B maritime energy business with no consumer visibility.

Saks Global is the US luxury retail group formed in December 2024 when Saks Fifth Avenue's owner HBC acquired Neiman Marcus Group, bringing together Saks Fifth Avenue, Neiman Marcus, Bergdorf Goodman and Saks OFF 5TH, headquartered in New York. Amazon and Salesforce were investors. It sells designer fashion, beauty and homeware to wealthy shoppers, but it has faced severe vendor payment and liquidity strain since 2025. Strong luxury retail brands in the US.

about: Pacaso is a San Francisco-based proptech company, founded in 2020 by Austin Allison and Spencer Rascoff, that sells fractional shares of luxury second homes, typically 1/8 to 1/2 of a property, to buyers who co-own through an LLC and use it part of the year. It earns sales commissions and management fees, with homes in the US, Mexico, Europe and Canada. It has raised about $1.7 billion in funding including debt. Visible among high-net-worth buyers.

Dubai real estate developer DarGlobal, a unit of Dar Al Arkan, developing luxury branded residences such as Trump International projects in Jeddah, Dubai and the Maldives. Listed on London AIM. Customers are wealthy property buyers. The parent, Dar Al Arkan, is a Saudi Arabian developer listed on Tadawul, and DarGlobal markets its branded projects internationally under licences such as Trump and Versace. Brand moderately visible in luxury property.

wiki.title: DarGlobal
wiki.text: Dar Global PLC is a real estate development company headquartered in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, and is publicly listed on the London Stock Exchange (LSE). The company began trading on the LSE on February 28, 2023, becoming the first Saudi company to be listed on the main market of the London Stock Exchange.

about: Extell Development Company is a New York real estate developer behind skyscrapers and condominiums such as Central Park Tower, One Manhattan Square and the Brooklyn Tower tower plans. Founded and led by Gary Barnett, it builds and sells luxury residential, hotel and commercial projects, mainly in Manhattan. Privately held. Crunchbase shows about $3 billion in funding. Known in New York property circles, low national consumer brand awareness.

about: Compass is a US residential real estate brokerage and technology platform, founded in 2012, whose agents buy and sell homes using its software for marketing, client management and listings. It earns commission on home sales and agreed in 2025 to combine with Anywhere Real Estate, owner of Coldwell Banker, Century 21 and Sotheby's International Realty. Headquartered in New York and listed on the NYSE (COMP). Strong B2C brand in affluent US markets.

Global Technical Realty provides build-to-suit data centres and technical real estate for hyperscalers and AI customers. Based in London, England, it is classed under data centres and information technology and has raised about $1.9 billion. Customers are cloud and AI providers leasing capacity, and revenue is rent and services. B2B infrastructure with no consumer visibility.

about: Soloviev Group is a New York-based real estate development company founded by Sergey Soloviev that is focused on luxury residential and mixed-use projects in the US and internationally, including Moscow-origin and Miami developments. Revenue is property sales and development fees. Privately held, with a modest public profile outside the property industry.
cb_desc: Soloviev Group is a global business focused on real estat...

about: WeWork is a New York flexible workspace company that rents shared office space, private offices and memberships to freelancers, startups and corporates, with locations in cities around the world. Founded in 2010 by Adam Neumann, it was backed by SoftBank, abandoned its 2019 IPO, listed via SPAC in 2021, and filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2023. It emerged as a private company in 2024. Strong brand awareness among professionals.

wiki.title: WeWork
wiki.text: WeWork Inc. is an American company headquartered in New York City that provides coworking spaces, including physical and virtual shared spaces, in approximately 600 buildings in 125 cities.

about: Brookfield India Real Estate Trust is a Mumbai-listed REIT, sponsored by Brookfield, that owns commercial office parks such as Candor TechSpace in Noida, Gurugram and Kolkata, and Downtown Powai. Tenants are multinational corporations and IT firms. It trades on the Indian exchanges (BIRET). A financial real estate vehicle with no consumer brand. Tenants include multinational technology and services firms. Distribution income flows to unit holders, and the trust has no consumer brand, though its office parks are well known locally.

Lodha Group is a Mumbai real estate developer, India's largest by sales, building premium residential towers and townships such as Palava in Mumbai, London projects, and commercial and industrial parks. Customers are homebuyers. Listed in India as Macrotech Developers (LODHA). Consumer-facing brand in Mumbai, with growing visibility. Revenue comes from property sales, and the company has delivered many thousands of apartments. It is a premium consumer brand in Mumbai, with heavy advertising.

McDermott is a Houston-based engineering and construction company for offshore and subsea energy projects, one of the largest in the sector, which filed for Chapter 11 in 2020 and was restructured, with lenders taking ownership. The input fields look scrambled (real estate, early-stage tech), so this may reflect a different entity. B2B energy contractor. Details are uncertain. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Onni Group of Companies is a Vancouver-based private real estate developer and landlord that builds and manages condominiums, rental towers, commercial and mixed-use projects in Canada and the United States, including Vancouver, Los Angeles and Seattle. The input shows funding of about 900 million dollars. Customers are homebuyers, tenants and commercial occupiers. It is privately held and visible mostly through local development signage rather than national consumer advertising.

about: Madison, New Jersey-based residential real estate services company (formerly Realogy), listed on the NYSE (HOUS), owning brands Coldwell Banker, Century 21, Sotheby's International Realty, ERA, Better Homes and Gardens Real Estate and Corcoran, and the Cartus relocation business. It also owns title and mortgage joint ventures and earns franchise fees and commissions. Revenue about 5.7 billion dollars. Agreed to be acquired by Compass in 2025. Strong consumer brands.

Irvine, California-based commercial real estate firm, offering investment and development services, per its Crunchbase listing. Funding shown is $1.42 billion. B2B brand with low public awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Privately held New York real estate company led by Charles Kushner, developing and owning residential, office, retail and mixed-use property mainly in New York, New Jersey and the US Northeast and Southeast, with a large multifamily portfolio of tens of thousands of apartments. Revenue comes from rents, development and property sales. Family-owned and private. Name is publicly known mainly through the family's political connections; limited consumer brand presence, so sponsorship appetite is uncertain.

about: Delos is a New York-based wellness real estate and technology company, founded by Paul Scialla, which designs buildings and products for human health, such as the WELL building standard concept with the International WELL Building Institute, and Delos Living. It has raised about $580 million. B2B with niche recognition.

Selina is a hospitality brand for digital nomads and travellers, based in London, running hostels, hotels, coworking and eco-lodges in about 25 countries, mainly in Latin America and Europe. It listed on Nasdaq (SLNA) through a SPAC merger in 2022, then ran into heavy losses and restructuring in 2023-24. Known among backpackers and remote workers, with a weak financial position.

about: Rockefeller Capital Management is a New York-based private wealth manager, formed in 2018 around the Rockefeller family's financial advisory business, offering wealth management, asset management and strategic advisory services for wealthy families, endowments and institutions. It manages roughly 100 billion dollars. Investors include Viking Global and Rockefeller family interests. Privately held. Recognised financial name with a heritage brand and strong visibility among affluent clients, but not a consumer sponsor.

Quinn Residences is a real estate company in the Commercial Real Estate sector, with Crunchbase showing an Atlanta, Georgia location and an entry that begins with providing residential-related real estate services. Total funding is shown as $2.75 billion, latest in November 2024. The scale, owners, properties and customers cannot be confirmed from the input, and the size of the funding figure suggests a platform-type fund or investment programme rather than an operating brand.
